source: Rice Straw Storage and its Nutritional Value, USAID Feed the Future / Kansas State University / CE SAIN Agricultural Extension Program, Royal University of Agriculture, First Edition 2021
text:
Rice straw (ចំបើង) is the dry-season cattle feed most Cambodian smallholders already stockpile after harvest, but its feed value depends heavily on how it's stored, not just on the variety it came from. A comparison of two common storage methods -- open-pile stacking versus wrapping the stack in a tarp/plastic cover -- found that tarp-wrapped straw retained crude protein, and kept fiber quality (NDF, ADF) much closer to its fresh-cut level after around 148 days of storage, than straw left in an open, exposed pile, which lost more nutritional value to rain exposure, sun bleaching, and mold over the same period.

Practical guidance: after harvest, dry the straw down to roughly 12% moisture, then stack it off wet ground and cover or wrap it with a tarp rather than leaving it as a bare, exposed pile. The covered stack keeps better nutrient density, resists mold and spoilage-driven feed refusal by cattle, and gives more reliable dry-season nutrition per bundle of straw than an equivalent uncovered stack -- a low-cost storage change with a real difference in feed value, not just tidiness.
